equity_bridge.item: VECV 54.40% equity stake at 15x Eicher's FY2026 share of VECV profit
equity_bridge.note: Rs 797.81 crore share of JV profit (FY2026 consolidated P&L) x 15 = Rs 11,967 crore. 15x is a discount to listed CV peers (Ashok Leyland mid-20s P/E) for CV cyclicality (FY26 share of profit is near cycle high, FY20-22 ran at Rs 30-60 crore), joint control with Volvo and a low dividend payout (Rs 217.60 crore received FY26). Cross-check: 3.2x the Rs 3,723 crore equity-method carrying value. ~Rs 435/share.

equity_bridge.item: Bill discounting on behalf of related party (VECV) at book
equity_bridge.note: Note 10 'Loans / Bill discounting' Rs 451.24 crore at 31-Mar-2026; interest earned is in other income, already outside the owner-FCF flows.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 17.0% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 32.5% (>30% relative divergence). The 5yr window starts at FY2021, a COVID-depressed base (EPS 49.24, revenue down 5%), which inflates EPS and FCF CAGRs; equity compounds slower because ~35% of profit is now paid out (FY26 dividends Rs 1,920 crore). The 3yr figures (revenue 17.5%, EPS 23.6%, equity 18.7%) are the cleaner read.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income is already outside OCF). SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are essentially identical (17.9% vs 18.1% 3yr) -- SBC is immaterial (~0.24% of revenue) and is not funding the growth. Revenue/EBITDA/FCF are Royal Enfield only; VECV is equity-accounted and outside these series, while EPS includes the JV share of profit.

scenario_narratives.base: Royal Enfield keeps its near-monopoly below 350cc and grows with India's premiumisation: FY27 +17% as Q1's +31.5% laps the pre-GST base and the post-GST festive surge caps H2, then double-digit volume growth (management guidance, capacity to ~2m units by FY28) plus price/mix, fading to 7% nominal. EBITDA margin holds ~25% as Flying Flea start-up losses and commodity costs offset 450-platform mix. Capex steps up to 6.5% of revenue for Cheyyar and Andhra Pradesh, then normalises. VECV is worth 15x its FY26 profit share; Rs 19,949 crore of treasury is added at book.
scenario_narratives.bull: The GST cut proves a structural step up in affordability (enquiry-to-booking 20% -> ~30%) and the >350cc slab is also cut to 18%, reopening the 450/650 range. Exports (Brazil CKD #2, Mexico CKD, SAARC, UK/EU) compound 20%+ and Flying Flea finds a profitable niche, so growth runs 21% in FY27 and stays double-digit through FY32. Operating leverage on new capacity and better mix lift EBITDA back to 27%, still below the FY18 30.5% peak.
scenario_narratives.bear: The GST pull-forward unwinds: FY27 slows to +11% as the post-cut surge is lapped, then mid-single-digit growth as Bajaj-Triumph/KTM and Hero-Harley take the 350-500cc band, where RE already has only ~27-28%. Flying Flea burns capital against Ola/Ather/TVS/Bajaj incumbents, and price cuts plus commodity inflation push EBITDA down to 21% (the FY21-22 trough), while the board-approved capacity programme runs anyway and capex peaks at 6.8%. VECV is held at the same bridge value; a CV downturn there is part of why the bear weight is not lower.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Royal Enfield is valued as an INR owner-FCF stream at a 12% INR cost of equity; the 54.4% VECV stake and the net-cash treasury are added separately. Treasury income is already outside OCF in Eicher's own cash flow statement, so it is not deducted again. SBC is immaterial, so the house and street bases nearly coincide. Leases are treated as operating cost and kept out of net debt.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY2027 growth is the most exposed driver: Q2 FY27 (due mid-November 2026) laps the post-GST festive surge and will show whether the step-up was demand or pull-forward
Terminal value depends on a 5% nominal INR perpetuity and an 18x cap; each 1pp of terminal growth moves value by a few hundred rupees per share
VECV is valued at one multiple on a near-cycle-high profit share; CV downturns historically cut it by 80-90% (FY20-22)
Margin path: the 350-500cc competition and Flying Flea losses could hold EBITDA below 24% for longer than the base assumes
Deferred tax on unrealised treasury gains is not deducted (small overstatement)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: FY2026 AR EPS note weighted-average diluted 274,763,316 (line 24098); Q1 FY2027 results 274.805m. Held FLAT -- SBC (ESOP/RSU, ~0.24% of revenue) is expensed in the flows; small ESOP allotments (Rs 12 cr FY26) are the SBC, not separate issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 consolidated cash flow 'Expenses recognised in respect of equity-settled share-based payments' Rs 55.09 crore (AR FY2026 consolidated CFS); India net-settles nothing, so equity-award taxes are nil (EquityAwardTaxes kpi = 0).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T09:59:17Z (15:29 IST, last minute of the NSE regular session, Friday close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR, the currency of the flows. India 10-year G-sec ~6.4-6.5% (Nov 2026); India ERP ~6.5% (mature-market ~4.3% plus country premium); beta ~0.85 for a net-cash, consumer-discretionary two-wheeler OEM -> cost of equity ~12.0%. Effectively zero debt (Rs 319 crore working-capital/SIPCOT soft loans against Rs 19,949 crore treasury) so WACC = cost of equity = 12.0%. Identical to BAJAJ-AUTO.NS in this folder so the two Indian 2W OEMs compare directly. Same WACC in all three scenarios: competitive, EV-execution and commodity risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights. Terminal growth is NOMINAL INR (India ~4% CPI target plus modest real growth).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: FY2026 lease cash Rs 74.30 crore (principal 62.22 + interest 12.08, consolidated CFS financing) = 0.32% of revenue charged via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (Rs 194.94 crore) EXCLUDED from net debt; da_pct is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (FY26 D&A 840.37 less ROU depreciation 66.18 = 774.19 crore = 3.31% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: None needed. Consolidated profit attributable to non-controlling interests is nil (FY2026 consolidated P&L). The '9.99% non-controlling interests' text in the AR (lines 17004/23600) is inside VECV's own summarised financial information, i.e. it sits within the equity-accounted JV and is already net in Eicher's share of profit.
inputs.vecv_treatment: VE Commercial Vehicles (54.40% economic interest, joint control with Volvo) is EQUITY-ACCOUNTED: consolidated revenue, EBITDA and cash flows are Royal Enfield (+ small subsidiaries) only; 'Share of profit of joint venture' (Rs 797.81 crore FY26) is below EBITDA and removed from OCF, and JV dividends (Rs 217.60 crore FY26) sit in investing. The owner-FCF flows therefore exclude VECV entirely, and the stake is added once in equity_bridge at 15x Eicher's FY2026 share of VECV profit (matching-asset rule: income out of flows, asset into bridge). Not double-counted: neither the JV carrying value (Rs 3,723 crore) nor its dividends appear anywhere else.
inputs.treasury_composition: Rs crore at 31-Mar-2026 (consolidated BS + notes 9, 11, 14, 15): other investments non-current 10,940.48 (debt mutual funds, bonds, 181 crore equity incl. strategic stakes) + current investments 2,831.97 + cash 234.29 + other bank balances 21.75 + bank deposits >12m 2,908.99 + bank deposits <12m 3,011.97 = 19,949.45 crore = INR 199,494.5m. Less borrowings 201.63 NC + 117.38 current = 319.01 crore (INR 3,190.1m). Net cash INR 196,304.4m (~Rs 714/share). Treasury income (FY26 FVTPL gains 745.55 + interest 473.86 crore) is already excluded from OCF by the company's own CFS (it is an adjustment out of PBT), so interest_income is 0 in the owner-FCF bridge -- deducting it again would double-strip. Deferred tax on unrealised MF gains (inside the Rs 658 crore DTL) is not deducted: a small overstatement of the treasury, likely < Rs 10/share.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'), with VECV valued separately in the bridge -- the business straddles an operating company (Royal Enfield, consolidated) and a 54.4% equity-accounted JV stake, so the parts are valued separately and summed. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). FY0 = FY2026 (year to 31-Mar-2026). Base revenue = consolidated revenue from operations Rs 23,407.56 crore. FY2026 consolidated EBITDA ex other income = Rs 5,785.07 crore (24.71%); plus SBC 55.09 = adj. EBITDA 24.95% pre-SBC. Q1 FY2027 (Apr-Jun 2026): revenue Rs 6,632.42 crore (+31.5% y/y), EBITDA 1,590.62 crore (23.98%), D&A 277.55 crore (4.2% of revenue, new Cheyyar/EV-plant capacity and 450-platform amortisation). Q2 FY2027 results (due mid-November 2026) are not yet on disk; the FY2027 growth driver is the judgment most exposed to them. Balance sheet anchor is the 31-Mar-2026 annual: Indian Q1 results carry no balance sheet; the 30-Sep-2026 half-year statement of assets and liabilities will replace it. Working capital: Royal Enfield runs negative working capital (trade payables + contract liabilities Rs 3,139 crore vs inventory + receivables Rs 2,321 crore); FY26 working-capital release Rs 278 crore on a Rs 4,537 crore revenue increase (6%), FY25 Rs 211 crore on Rs 1,940 crore (11%) -> wc_capture +5% base. Cash tax: Indian new-regime statutory 25.168% on operating profit; no carryforwards. Buybacks: none ever -- the flat count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC expense, not by repurchases; SBC is small enough (0.24% of revenue) that house and street nearly coincide. Bill discounting on behalf of a related party (VECV, Rs 451.24 crore, note 10) is a financial asset whose income sits in treasury income, so it is added to the bridge at book.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 +17%: Q1 +31.5% laps a pre-GST-cut base; Q2-Q4 lap the post-GST festive surge (Rs 6,080-6,172 crore quarters), so H2 growth slows to ~10%. Then double-digit volume guidance plus ~3-4% price/mix fading to 7% nominal by FY36 (India premium-2W penetration plus exports).
base.margin_rationale: FY26 adj. EBITDA 24.95% pre-SBC, Q1 FY27 24.0% (commodity costs, Flying Flea start-up losses). Held at ~25%, below the FY18 peak of 30.5%: the 350-500cc band is contested by Bajaj-Triumph/KTM and Hero-Harley.
base.capex_rationale: FY26 capex 5.45% of revenue. Elevated to 6.5% for FY27-28 by board-approved Cheyyar (Rs 958 crore) and Andhra Pradesh greenfield (Rs 1,225 crore) plus EV platform intangibles, fading to 4.5% (still above D&A, consistent with 7% nominal growth).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): FY26-27 growth is flattered by a one-time GST step and the 350-500cc band is genuinely contested, while VECV (a cyclical, held at one bridge value) adds downside correlated with an Indian slowdown. No solvency risk, which keeps it from going higher: Rs 19,949 crore of treasury against Rs 319 crore of debt. Base 50%: management's double-digit volume guidance and board-approved capacity support it. Bull 30% (below 35%): it needs several independent things -- a >350cc GST cut, profitable EV entry and export compounding -- to all go right.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
